conv.n.sync_archived: Archived %1$d contact record(s); the server is at position %2$d.
conv.n.sync_pulled: Applied %1$d; skipped %2$d unreadable, %3$d older and %4$d own record(s). Position %5$d of %6$d.
conv.n.cannot_send: This conversation cannot be sent to.
conv.n.card_one_person: A contact card goes to one person, not to a group.
conv.n.card_own: That is this conversation's own contact.
conv.n.remove_self: You cannot remove yourself from the member list. To leave, use Leave group.
conv.n.reactions_unavailable: Reactions are not available in this conversation.
conv.n.reaction_pending: Reaction added here; it was not delivered yet.
conv.n.group_picture_refused: Not changed: only an admin can edit this group, or the file is not a picture.
conv.n.actions_unavailable: Message actions are not available in this conversation.
conv.n.edit_own_only: Only messages you sent can be edited.
conv.n.delete_own_only: Only messages you sent can be deleted.
conv.n.edited_pending: Message edited here; it was not delivered yet.
conv.n.deleted_pending: Message deleted here; it was not delivered yet.
conv.n.direct_only: This is only available in a conversation with one person.
conv.n.offline_on_untold: Your contact could not be told over the internet — that is what you just switched off. They will hear when a radio or a nearby device can carry it.
conv.n.offline_off_untold: Your contact has not been told yet.
conv.composer.bot: Bot messages are NOT end-to-end encrypted: the server can read them, and it already knows the group's name and every member. So this window does not put them behind the same text box as an encrypted conversation.
conv.composer.lora: Plain Meshtastic radio text, kept apart and marked unverified. Nobody's identity was checked, so there is no verified sender to reply to.
conv.send.refused_short: REFUSED — that text is itself an OSHI control message. Nothing was sent or stored; your text is still in the box.
conv.send.group_empty: NOT SENT — this group has nobody in it but you.
conv.send.group_none: NOT DELIVERED — 0 of %d members took it. None of them can be reached securely yet.
conv.send.group_partial: PARTIAL — %1$d of %2$d members took it. The others have not published their keys yet, so they cannot be reached.
conv.send.blocked_skipped: %d blocked member(s) were skipped, which is not a failure.
conv.send.blocked: NOT SENT — that contact is blocked. The message was not saved either.
conv.send.server_down_keys: NOT DELIVERED — the OSHI server is not answering right now, so your contact's keys could not be fetched. This is not about them. The message is saved and marked failed; try again when the connection is back.
conv.send.no_keys: NOT DELIVERED — this contact has not published their keys, so they cannot be reached yet. The message is saved and marked failed.
conv.send.server_down: NOT SENT — the OSHI server is not answering right now. This is a connection problem, not a setting of your account. The message is saved and marked failed.
conv.send.no_answer_yet: NOT SENT — the server has not answered yet, so sending stays closed for now. That is not a decision about your account; try again in a moment. The message is saved and marked failed.
conv.send.gate_closed: NOT SENT — sending is not open for this account yet. The message is saved and marked failed.
conv.send.refused_control: REFUSED — that text is an OSHI control message (a receipt, a typing signal, a reaction or an edit). Sending it would let the other side edit messages. Nothing was sent or stored; your text is still in the box.
conv.reach.no_keys: has not published keys — cannot be reached yet
pc.limits.ledger.note: What the desktop does differently from the phones, row by row, with the reference in the engineering ledger.
pc.ledger.calls.title: Calls to a phone
pc.ledger.calls.why: Voice and video calls work in this window and were measured live between two computers, also through a relay server. A call to an iPhone or an Android phone has not been tested yet, and neither has a call across a home router. The speaker was checked on a real machine; the microphone is deliberately not tested automatically.
pc.ledger.location.title: Sending your location or a check-in
pc.ledger.location.why: A computer has no GPS and OSHI does not fake one, so locations and check-ins can be received here but not sent. Places search works offline from maps on this disk, and contact cards do send. Over a LoRa radio, this computer can announce a position you type in.
pc.ledger.push.title: Push notifications
pc.ledger.push.why: Computers have no Apple or Google push service for OSHI. OSHI checks for messages while it runs, so nothing arrives while the computer sleeps, and the time between checks is the delay.
pc.ledger.screenshot.title: Blocking screenshots
pc.ledger.screenshot.why: macOS and Windows have a setting for it and Linux has none, but on macOS 15 and later screen recorders are reported to capture protected windows anyway. A switch promising a protection that does not hold would be a false security promise, so none is offered.
pc.ledger.watch.title: Apple Watch
pc.ledger.watch.why: A watch needs a paired iPhone. Nothing equivalent exists for a computer.
pc.ledger.phoneSync.title: Syncing history with your phone
pc.ledger.phoneSync.why: A new desktop profile can restore your identity from your phone's recovery key, but message history and groups do not come across yet: the phones do not write the signed archive this app requires. The older, unsigned archive is deliberately not used.
pc.ledger.loraBluetooth.title: Pairing a LoRa radio over Bluetooth
pc.ledger.loraBluetooth.why: The desktop runtime has no Bluetooth. Connect the radio with a USB cable (macOS, Linux) or over the network (TCP port 4403); on Windows, use the network. Reading radio and nearby messages does work: OSHI messages are decrypted and filed under their sender, and plain Meshtastic text gets its own thread marked unverified.
pc.ledger.bubbles.title: Bubble styles and link previews
pc.ledger.bubbles.why: Chat wallpapers exist and stay on this computer. Phones keep bubble styles on each device and never sync them, so a style chosen here would not show there. A link preview would make this app open a link a stranger sent, which reveals you to that website, so it is not done.
pc.ledger.media.title: Pictures, voice notes and videos
pc.ledger.media.why: Photos open as a thumbnail and full size, with their format and size read from the file itself. Limits of 64 MiB and 32 megapixels keep a stranger's file from exhausting memory, and a cut-off file is shown and labelled incomplete. Voice notes and videos play here; playback through a real speaker has not been tested automatically.
pc.ledger.groupAdmin.title: Advanced group administration
pc.ledger.groupAdmin.why: Sending to groups, creating, renaming, leaving, adding and removing members and changing roles all work here. The creator role cannot be given away. Rarer operations are only in the command console (/group) for now.
pc.ledger.bots.title: Bot channels
pc.ledger.bots.why: Bot channels are not encrypted at all, so this window gives them no text box. They can be used from the command console (/bot send), which repeats that warning on every send.
pc.ledger.controls.title: Reactions, edits, receipts and typing
pc.ledger.controls.why: Reactions, edits and deletions you receive are shown, and you can react, and edit or delete your own messages. Opening a conversation sends a read receipt when your privacy settings allow it, and typing is shown in both directions.
pc.ledger.checkpoint.title: Sync checkpoint
pc.ledger.checkpoint.why: Pushing and pulling the contact archive is under Account. A sync checkpoint stays in the command console because it deletes items on the server that your other devices may not have fetched yet. Scheduled messages, the radio and account deletion all have their own screens.
pc.ledger.languages.title: Languages
pc.ledger.languages.why: The app ships in 34 languages, and every sentence this window shows is translated into each of them.
